theme: The Sopranos: family, therapy, and the sacred cold cut
callback: The gabagool is a state of mind

events.text: So I finally finished The Sopranos. All six seasons. I feel like I need a therapist and a deli platter.
Welcome to the family. I told you - it's not a show, it's a lifestyle. You start saying 'gabagool' and suddenly you're judging everyone's capicola.
It's pronounced 'gabagool'? I thought that was just a meme.
It's a dialect thing. Southern Italian immigrants in New Jersey said 'capicola' so fast it became 'gabagool.' Like how Toronto says 'Tronno.'
So I've been eating gabagool my whole life and didn't know it. That's... actually profound.
You're having an existential crisis over cold cuts. This is the most Sopranos thing that's ever happened to you.
I can't stop thinking about Dr. Melfi. Like, Tony's in therapy, lying to her, having panic attacks about ducks... and I'm here stressed about whether to get a double-double or a triple-triple.
That's your panic attack? The duck thing is iconic. He sees a family of ducks leave his pool and it unravels him.
Because the ducks represented his family! And they left! That's the whole show in one image.
Okay, Dr. Melfi. Next you'll tell me the pine barrens episode is a metaphor for existential isolation.
It IS! They're lost in the woods, no cell service, and they might have killed a guy who was maybe a Russian interior decorator. It's purgatory with snow.
You're one Timbit away from writing a dissertation.
Okay, No Thrills has a whole deli section. This is my gabagool moment.
You're going to stand here and pronounce it like a mob boss, aren't you.
Gabagool. Gabagool. It's like a meditation.
Did somebody say gabagool? I once tried to import a whole leg of prosciutto from Jersey on the TTC. Got stopped at Spadina. They thought it was a weapon.
Kessler, of course you did.

The trick is to wrap it in a Canada Goose jacket. Insulated. Discreet. Smells like a deli in a snowsuit. Anyway, the gabagool here is 30% off if you buy the family pack. Family pack. Like the Sopranos. It's a sign.
I'm buying the family pack.
We are not a family of six, Alan.
You are now.
Okay, I've been thinking. Tony Soprano's whole thing is that he can't talk to his family about his feelings, so he pays a therapist. But he lies to her too.
So the one person he's supposed to be honest with... he can't be honest with.
Right. And the ducks, the panic attacks, the gabagool - it's all about trying to feed something that's starving.
That's... actually really sad. And you got there from a deli counter.
I got there from you. You're the Dr. Melfi to my Tony, except you don't charge me and you actually laugh at my jokes.
And I don't have to worry about you whacking anyone. Usually.
Only the gabagool.
You know, the show's real lesson? Family is complicated, but you show up. And you share the cold cuts.
Then here's to us. And to the family pack.
